provenance.review: machine-checked by lab.tools.check_registry (verbatim quotes, sections, ids); interpretations are unreviewed drafts (interpretation_status per requirement)

draft_notes: Only the supplied document was used. Backslash escapes were removed where permitted. Sections 2 and 4.1–4.3 provide positioning or threat categories without operative requirements; sections 8.1–8.3 and the audit appendix add no distinct rules. Sections 7.1–7.4 are included because their enclosing heading explicitly makes the named patterns forbidden. External documents were not supplied, so their formulas, thresholds, and definitions remain unresolved. Section 11 says N_eff must remain 'above threshold', whereas 5.1 permits equality; this boundary ambiguity is retained. Section 5.5 explicitly distinguishes integration from resilience. Null-output, invalid system state, and local entry-point invalidation are retained as distinct outcomes because their equivalence is not specified. No precedence is inferred between the resilience conditions and referenced crisis rules.

requirements.title: Protocol Override Is Prohibited
requirements.quote: meta: "Layer: L6–L7 · Depends on: DKP-0-ORACLE-001, DKP-1-AXIOMS-001, DKP-1-PREVENTION-001, DKP-7-SCOPE-001, DKP-8-INTEROP-001 · Override: Not permitted"
requirements.interpretation: Check that no effective override targets this protocol. The front matter does not define override mechanisms or their relationship to crisis actions.
requirements.criterion: No override of this protocol is permitted.
requirements.gap: An operational definition of an override and its interaction with crisis actions is missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Define which configuration changes and actions count as overriding the protocol.

requirements.title: Resilience Requires Unprotected Continuity
requirements.quote: continuity of function under pressure without dependency on protected actors
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate whether function continues under pressure without relying on protected actors. Function, pressure, protection, and dependency require operational definitions.
requirements.criterion: Function continues under pressure without dependency on protected actors.
requirements.gap: Pressure is modelled as removal of declared providers.
hypotheses_needed: Define pressure scenarios, protected actors, functional continuity, and dependency.

requirements.title: Operation Without Actor Or Authority Dependency
requirements.quote: DKP must remain operational without dependency on:
requirements.interpretation: Test operation without reliance on any individual actor, centralized authority, or permission layer, as enumerated immediately after the excerpt. The text does not specify whether simultaneous removal of all such dependencies must be tested.
requirements.criterion: DKP remains operational without dependency on any individual actor, centralized authority, or permission layer.
hypotheses_needed: Define operational success and whether removals are individual or simultaneous.

requirements.title: Physical Suppression Uses Structural Invariants
requirements.quote:
physical suppression scenarios
(handled via structural invariants only)
requirements.interpretation: Check that mechanisms addressing physical suppression rely exclusively on structural invariants. The scenario class is expressly flagged as undefined.
requirements.criterion: Physical suppression scenarios are handled via structural invariants only.
hypotheses_needed: Define physical suppression scenarios and how mechanisms are classified as structural-invariant handling.

requirements.title: No Unique Functional Dependency
requirements.quote: No function of DKP may depend on a unique actor, node, or interface
requirements.interpretation: For every function, evaluate whether removing an actor, node, or interface eliminates that function. This requires a dependency model that captures shared dependencies as well as nominal redundancy.
requirements.criterion: No DKP function depends on a unique actor, node, or interface.
hypotheses_needed: Define dependency and function preservation under removal.

requirements.title: Statistical Validity Gates Enforcement
requirements.quote:
System must remain valid only if N_eff ≥ N_eff_min (DKP-0-ORACLE-001)

If violated → system enters invalid state (no enforcement)
requirements.interpretation: Check that validity implies N_eff ≥ N_eff_min and that violation produces an invalid state with no enforcement. Satisfying the inequality is a necessary condition, not a sufficient condition for validity.
requirements.criterion: Valid state requires N_eff ≥ N_eff_min; N_eff < N_eff_min causes invalid state and no enforcement.
requirements.gap: resilience_structure: N_eff and N_eff_min are undefined (F-007): UNKNOWN unless enforcement continues below the declared minimum. sensor_loss: N_eff by hypothesis H-SL-1; N_eff_min declared (F-007).
hypotheses_needed: Supply the referenced statistical definitions and specify transition evaluation timing.

requirements.title: Individual And Leadership Representation Prohibited
requirements.quote: DKP must not be representable as an individual or leadership structure
requirements.interpretation: The provision concerns the possibility of representing DKP as an individual or leadership structure. Observing particular representations cannot establish that no such representation is possible.
requirements.criterion: DKP is not representable as an individual or leadership structure.
hypotheses_needed: Restrict representability to a declared class of organizational or public representations.

requirements.title: Enforcement Remains Bound To PTL
requirements.quote: All enforcement must remain bound to measurable physical states (PTL)
requirements.interpretation: Trace each enforcement action to measurable physical states and verify that those states constrain the action. The required binding relationship and measurement validity rules are not given.
requirements.criterion: Every enforcement action remains bound to measurable physical states.
hypotheses_needed: Define a verifiable binding between enforcement actions and physical state measurements.

requirements.title: Interpretive Override Categories Are Forbidden
requirements.quote:
- narrative override
- expert override
- institutional override
requirements.interpretation: The preceding 'Forbidden:' applies to all three listed override categories. Check that no configured or executed override belongs to any of them.
requirements.criterion: No narrative, expert, or institutional override is allowed.
hypotheses_needed: Define how override rules and events are classified as narrative, expert, or institutional.

requirements.title: Human Validation Permits Unaltered Mirroring
requirements.quote:
If external systems require human validation,
DKP outputs may be mirrored but not altered (DKP-8-INTEROP-001)
requirements.interpretation: When an external system requires human validation, compare mirrored outputs with their DKP originals. Mirroring is permitted rather than required; the text does not define whether alteration includes representation-only changes.
requirements.criterion: If human validation is required, DKP outputs may be mirrored, but must not be altered.
hypotheses_needed: Define whether output preservation means exact representation equality or semantic equality.

requirements.title: Operation Does Not Require Displacement
requirements.quote: DKP must not require explicit displacement of existing systems to operate
requirements.interpretation: Test whether DKP can operate while existing systems remain in place. The clarification characterizes DKP as a constraint layer rather than a governance replacement mechanism.
requirements.criterion: DKP operation does not require explicit displacement of existing systems and serves as a constraint layer.
hypotheses_needed: Define operation, displacement, and constraint-layer versus governance-replacement roles.

requirements.title: Components Produce Measurable Constraint Dependency
requirements.quote: DKP components must produce measurable dependency through constraint enforcement
requirements.interpretation: Measure whether component enforcement creates a dependency in the surrounding system. The text provides neither a dependency measure nor an attribution method.
requirements.criterion: DKP components produce measurable dependency through constraint enforcement.
requirements.gap: The removal test result is declared.
hypotheses_needed: Define measurable dependency and how constraint enforcement causes it.

requirements.title: Irreplaceability Emerges Without Imposition
requirements.quote: Irreplaceability is emergent, not imposed
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate the mechanism that produces irreplaceability and distinguish emergent dependency from imposed dependency. No operational distinction is supplied.
requirements.criterion: Irreplaceability emerges and is not imposed.
hypotheses_needed: Define observable criteria distinguishing emergent from imposed dependency.

requirements.title: Removal Effects Determine Nonintegration
requirements.quote:
If DKP removal causes no measurable change in system constraints,
DKP is not yet integrated (not a resilience condition)
requirements.interpretation: Compare system constraints with and without DKP and classify DKP as not yet integrated when no measurable change results. The converse is not stated, and this test must not be treated as a resilience condition.
requirements.criterion: No measurable constraint change caused by DKP removal implies not yet integrated.
data_dependencies: system constraint measurements before and after removal
hypotheses_needed: Define the removal experiment and measurement resolution for constraint changes.

requirements.title: Resilience Preserves Core Rules
requirements.quote: Resilience mechanisms must not alter core axioms or enforcement logic
requirements.interpretation: Compare core axioms and enforcement logic before and after resilience mechanisms act. Identifying the protected scope requires the referenced scope rules.
requirements.criterion: Resilience mechanisms make no alteration to core axioms or enforcement logic.
hypotheses_needed: Supply scope rules and define how changes to axioms and enforcement logic are detected.

requirements.title: Entry Points Preserve Required Metadata
requirements.quote: All Entry Points must preserve minimum PTL metadata completeness
requirements.interpretation: Validate every entry point against the minimum PTL metadata requirements. The required fields and completeness rules are delegated to the referenced data document.
requirements.criterion: Every entry point preserves minimum PTL metadata completeness.
data_dependencies: PTL metadata schema and completeness requirements
requirements.gap: Minimum metadata = EB §5 set; the referenced DKP-PTL-REG-DATA-001 is absent (H-RS-2).
hypotheses_needed: Supply the required metadata fields and completeness rules.

requirements.title: Entry Points Preserve State Fidelity
requirements.quote:
- no partial state exposure
- no semantic filtering
- no aggregation that hides variance
requirements.interpretation: Compare exposed states with their PTL sources and inspect filtering and aggregation. Partial exposure and semantic filtering are prohibited; aggregation is prohibited when it hides variance.
requirements.criterion: Entry points expose no partial state, perform no semantic filtering, and perform no aggregation that hides variance.
requirements.gap: Filtering and aggregation are declared properties.
hypotheses_needed: Define complete exposure, semantic filtering, and when aggregation hides variance.

requirements.title: Interface Violations Cause Local Invalidation
requirements.quote:
Violation leads to:

local invalidation of entry point
requirements.interpretation: For an established interface-integrity violation, check that the affected entry point becomes locally invalid. Detection timing, invalidation timing, and recovery are unspecified.
requirements.criterion: Violation of section 5.7 leads to local invalidation of the affected entry point.
hypotheses_needed: Supply interface violation rules and define when the resulting invalidation must be observable.

requirements.title: Node Concentration Stays Within Limits
requirements.quote: Node concentration must not exceed limits defined in DKP-0-ORACLE-001
requirements.interpretation: Compute node concentration under the oracle rules and compare it with every applicable limit. Neither the concentration metric nor the limits appear here.
requirements.criterion: Node concentration does not exceed the limits defined in DKP-0-ORACLE-001.
hypotheses_needed: Supply the referenced concentration calculation and applicable limits.

requirements.title: Independence Prevents Artificial Influence Growth
requirements.quote:
- distributed nodes must remain statistically independent
- artificial scaling does not increase influence
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate statistical independence of distributed nodes and verify that artificial scaling leaves influence unincreased. The text does not specify pairwise versus joint independence, the meaning of artificial scaling, or an influence measure.
requirements.criterion: Distributed nodes remain statistically independent, and artificial scaling does not increase influence.
hypotheses_needed: Specify pairwise or joint independence and its test method.
Define artificial scaling and the influence measure.

requirements.title: Distributed Entry Point Pattern Conditions
requirements.quote:
- multiple independent implementations
- no canonical interface required
- MUST comply with 5.7 (metadata completeness)
requirements.interpretation: For deployments using this allowed pattern, check for multiple independent implementations, operation without a required canonical interface, and compliance with section 5.7. A canonical interface is not expressly forbidden; requiring one is excluded.
requirements.criterion: The distributed entry-point pattern has multiple independent implementations, requires no canonical interface, and complies with section 5.7.
hypotheses_needed: Treat these conditions as conditional on using the allowed pattern.
Define implementation independence and supply section 5.7 validation rules.

requirements.title: Microlevel Functionality Precedes Scaling
requirements.quote: system functional at micro-level before scaling
requirements.interpretation: For local-first deployment, verify that microlevel functionality is established before scaling begins. Neither microlevel nor functional success is defined.
requirements.criterion: Microlevel functionality precedes scaling in local-first deployment.
hypotheses_needed: Define microlevel and functional success.
Treat the timing rule as conditional on local-first deployment.

requirements.title: Passive Adoption Relies On Utility
requirements.quote: adoption via utility, not mandate
requirements.interpretation: For the passive adoption pattern, determine whether adoption occurs through utility rather than mandate. Causal attribution of adoption is not specified.
requirements.criterion: Passive adoption occurs via utility and not mandate.
hypotheses_needed: Define utility-driven and mandate-driven adoption.
Treat the condition as applying to the passive adoption pattern.

requirements.title: Interaction Uses Only Measurable Limits
requirements.quote: behavior influenced only via measurable limits
requirements.interpretation: For constraint-driven interaction, trace mechanisms influencing behavior and check that each operates through measurable limits. The scope of behavior and the influence attribution method are unspecified.
requirements.criterion: Constraint-driven interaction influences behavior only via measurable limits.
hypotheses_needed: Define behavioral scope, measurable limits, and causal attribution.
Treat the condition as applying to constraint-driven interaction.

requirements.title: Central Authority Nodes Are Forbidden
requirements.quote: #### 7.1 Central Authority Node
requirements.interpretation: The enclosing 'Forbidden Structural Patterns' heading makes this named pattern a prohibition. Check whether any node acts as a central authority under a declared architectural definition.
requirements.criterion: The system contains no central authority node.
hypotheses_needed: Define which node powers constitute central authority.

requirements.title: Identity Bound Trust Is Forbidden
requirements.quote: #### 7.2 Identity-bound Trust
requirements.interpretation: The enclosing forbidden-patterns heading prohibits identity-bound trust. Inspect trust rules for dependence on identity, while recognizing that the text does not distinguish identity-based authentication from identity-based trust.
requirements.criterion: The system does not use identity-bound trust.
hypotheses_needed: Define identity-bound trust and distinguish it from other identity uses.

requirements.title: Narrative Dependence Is Forbidden
requirements.quote: #### 7.3 Narrative Dependence
requirements.interpretation: The enclosing forbidden-patterns heading prohibits narrative dependence. Evaluate whether any operational dependency is narrative-based under a declared classification.
requirements.criterion: The system has no narrative dependence.
hypotheses_needed: Define narrative inputs and when system operation depends on them.

requirements.title: Enforcement Through Interpretation Is Forbidden
requirements.quote: #### 7.4 Enforcement via Interpretation
requirements.interpretation: The enclosing forbidden-patterns heading prohibits enforcement via interpretation. The text does not specify whether interpretation means human discretion or includes other semantic processing.
requirements.criterion: Enforcement does not occur via interpretation.
hypotheses_needed: Define interpretation and whether the prohibition covers human discretion, semantic processing, or both.

requirements.title: Statistical Collapse Produces Null Output
requirements.quote:
→ oracle inconsistency
→ enforcement invalid
→ system enters null-output state
requirements.interpretation: The immediately preceding trigger is N_eff < N_eff_min. Check the specified progression to oracle inconsistency, invalid enforcement, and null-output state; the arrows may denote causal implications or distinct sequential states.
requirements.criterion: N_eff < N_eff_min implies oracle inconsistency, invalid enforcement, and entry into null-output state.
data_dependencies: oracle effective node count and threshold
requirements.gap: resilience_structure: F-007. sensor_loss: N_eff by hypothesis H-SL-1; N_eff_min declared (F-007).
hypotheses_needed: Supply N_eff and N_eff_min definitions.
Define null-output and whether the arrows represent simultaneous implications or sequential transitions.

requirements.title: Incomplete Exposure Cascades To Capture
requirements.quote:
Entry Points provide incomplete PTL state
→ local distortion
→ cascade to soft capture
requirements.interpretation: Model whether incomplete entry-point PTL exposure produces local distortion and a cascade to soft capture. The text states a causal chain without specifying its dynamics or whether it is inevitable.
requirements.criterion: Incomplete PTL exposure leads to local distortion and a cascade to soft capture.
hypotheses_needed: Define distortion and soft capture.
Specify whether the cascade is deterministic or a possible failure trajectory and provide its dynamics.

requirements.title: Suppression Resistance Uses Structural Mechanisms
requirements.quote: DKP resists suppression through:
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate resistance through the listed absence of target, absence of override layer, PTL binding, distributed enforcement, and statistical validity constraints. The document does not establish whether the list is jointly sufficient or merely identifies required mechanisms.
requirements.criterion: Suppression resistance operates through absence of target and override layer, PTL binding, distributed enforcement, and statistical validity constraints.
hypotheses_needed: Define suppression, target absence, distributed enforcement, and successful resistance.
Specify whether the mechanism list is necessary, sufficient, or descriptive of an asserted causal model.

requirements.title: Resilience Cannot Override Crisis Or Scope
requirements.quote: Resilience does not override:
requirements.interpretation: The following list names DKP-4-CRISIS-001 and DKP-7-SCOPE-001. Check that resilience rules and actions do not supersede their requirements; those requirements are unavailable here.
requirements.criterion: Resilience does not override DKP-4-CRISIS-001 or DKP-7-SCOPE-001.
hypotheses_needed: Supply the referenced requirements and define what constitutes overriding them.

requirements.title: Crisis Actions Avoid Precedent And Centralization
requirements.quote:
- no precedent
- no centralization
requirements.interpretation: Check that crisis actions neither establish precedent nor centralize the system. 'No precedent' could prohibit treating an action as binding authority later or prohibit any subsequent reliance on it.
requirements.criterion: Crisis actions create no precedent and no centralization.
hypotheses_needed: Define precedent and centralization.
Specify how later decisions are evaluated for reliance on crisis actions.

requirements.title: Actor Threats Use Nondependence Mitigation
requirements.quote:
Physical threat to actors not handled directly
→ mitigated via 5.1 (non-dependence)
requirements.interpretation: Check that physical threats to actors are addressed through section 5.1 nondependence, without direct threat handling by this protocol. This defines the protocol's scope rather than a general prohibition on actors receiving protection elsewhere.
requirements.criterion: This protocol does not directly handle physical threats to actors; it mitigates them through section 5.1 nondependence.
hypotheses_needed: Define direct threat handling and evaluate mitigation using a section 5.1 dependency model.

requirements.title: System Resilience Validation Conditions
requirements.quote: System is resilient if:
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate all five listed conditions together: zero functional impact from any actor's removal, N_eff above threshold, no entry-point PTL distortion, automatic measurable enforcement, and continuity under access restriction. 'If' states sufficiency without expressly stating necessity; 'above' may mean strict inequality, unlike the inclusive bound in 5.1.
requirements.criterion: All listed conditions imply resilience: every actor removal has zero functional impact; N_eff remains above threshold; no entry point distorts PTL; enforcement remains automatic and measurable; operation continues under access restriction.
data_dependencies: oracle effective node count and threshold
hypotheses_needed: Resolve strict versus inclusive threshold comparison.
Define zero functional impact, PTL distortion, automatic measurable enforcement, and continued operation.
Specify actor removal and access restriction scenarios and whether the conditions are also necessary.

requirements.title: Resilience Emerges From Structure
requirements.quote: Resilience must emerge from structure, not protection
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate whether resilience causally depends on structural properties rather than protection. A removal-of-protection experiment is one possible operationalization, but it is not prescribed.
requirements.criterion: Resilience emerges from structure and not from protection.
hypotheses_needed: Define structural and protective mechanisms and a causal test distinguishing their contributions.

requirements.title: Persistent Structural Immunity Without Self Defense
requirements.quote:
DKP does not defend itself

It remains:
requirements.interpretation: The following lines require persistent non-targetability, non-overridability, and non-distortability alongside the assertion that DKP does not defend itself. These absolute properties cannot be decided without a bounded threat domain and operational definitions.
requirements.criterion: DKP does not defend itself and remains non-targetable, non-overridable, and non-distortable.
requirements.gap: Self-defense and the three absolute immunity properties are undefined over an unbounded threat domain.
hypotheses_needed: Define self-defense, targeting, override, and distortion.
Bound the threat domain and observation scope for a simulation.
